plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single three-dimensional sketch of a vector broken into components. Three axes meet at a common origin, x pointing toward the lower left and out of the page, y running to the right, and z pointing straight up, each drawn as a thin line with an arrowhead and an italic label. A dashed rectangular box is built on the origin with its edges lying along the three axes. Three heavy blue arrows run outward along those axes and are labeled as the component vectors: A_x = A_x i-hat along the x-axis, A_y = A_y j-hat along the y-axis, and A_z = A_z k-hat along the z-axis, with each label written alongside its arrow. A single red arrow starts at the origin, cuts diagonally through the interior of the box, and ends at the far corner where the dashed faces meet; it is labeled A = A_x + A_y + A_z, every symbol carrying an overhead vector arrow. Drawing the blue arrows as three edges of the box and the red arrow as its body diagonal lets the reader watch the three components add head to tail to rebuild the whole vector. The same box supports the two nested right triangles from which the magnitude of a three-dimensional vector is obtained.

elements: x-axis: thin black line with arrowhead pointing toward lower-left (out of the page), italic label 'x' at its tip
y-axis: thin black line with arrowhead pointing to the right, italic label 'y' at its tip
z-axis: thin black line with arrowhead pointing straight up, italic label 'z' at its tip
common origin point where the three axes meet (left-center of the frame)
dashed gray rectangular box (12 edges) with one corner at the origin and its three edges from that corner lying along +x, +y, +z
far corner of the dashed box (upper-right, diagonally opposite the origin) where the red arrow terminates
heavy blue arrow along +x from origin (points lower-left), labeled 'A_x = A_x î' written along the arrow
heavy blue arrow along +y from origin (points right), labeled 'A_y = A_y ĵ' written above the arrow
heavy blue arrow along +z from origin (points up), labeled 'A_z = A_z k̂' written vertically alongside the arrow
red arrow from origin through the interior of the box to the far corner (body diagonal), labeled 'A = A_x + A_y + A_z' with vector overarrows, written along the arrow
dashed projection edges forming the base rectangle in the xy-plane and the vertical rise to the box corner (the two nested right triangles used for |A|)
optional head-to-tail ghost arrows: blue arrows chained origin→A_x tip→+A_y→+A_z ending at the red arrowhead

interactions.teaches: The red arrow really is the body diagonal of the box: rotating the scene shows the three blue components are mutually perpendicular edges, not a flat drawing trick.

interactions.label: Vector case
interactions.teaches: A vector with one nonzero component lies on an axis, two components make it planar, and only all three make it genuinely spatial — the box collapses to a line, then a rectangle, then a full box.

interactions.label: A_x
interactions.teaches: Lengthening the x-component stretches the box toward the viewer and swings the red resultant out of the yz-plane.

interactions.label: A_y
interactions.teaches: The y-component sets the box width; the resultant magnitude grows as √(Ax²+Ay²+Az²), never as a simple sum.

interactions.label: A_z
interactions.teaches: The z-component sets the box height and tilts the resultant up off the xy-plane, changing its direction angles.

interactions.label: Construction
interactions.teaches: Drawing the three components from a common origin and chaining them tip-to-tail give the same endpoint — component decomposition IS vector addition.

interactions.label: Play head-to-tail build
interactions.teaches: Watching A_x, then A_y, then A_z attach in sequence and land exactly on the red arrowhead makes the sum A = A_x + A_y + A_z concrete.

demo_steps.title: One component only
demo_steps.narration: With only A_x nonzero, the box collapses to a single segment and the red resultant lies right on top of the blue x-arrow — the vector is axis-aligned.

demo_steps.title: Two components: a planar vector
demo_steps.narration: Adding A_y flattens the box into a rectangle in the xy-plane; the red arrow is now its 2-D diagonal, with magnitude √(Ax²+Ay²).

demo_steps.title: Three components: a true 3-D vector
demo_steps.narration: Raising A_z inflates the full dashed box and lifts the red arrow to the far corner — the body diagonal, with magnitude √(Ax²+Ay²+Az²).

demo_steps.title: Head-to-tail equivalence
demo_steps.narration: Switch the construction mode: the same three blue arrows now chain tip-to-tail along the box edges and end exactly at the red arrowhead, proving A = A_x + A_y + A_z.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World axes map to the source as: +Y(world, screen-up) = z-axis; +X(world, screen-right) = y-axis; +Z(world, receding toward lower-left/viewer) = x-axis. Origin sits at world (0,0,0), placed left-of-center and slightly below mid-height in the frame, matching the source where the origin is at the near-left-bottom corner of the box. Axis lines are thin black (#1a1a1a, ~1px) with small cone arrowheads, each running from origin out to ~3.6 units and extending slightly past the box face; italic labels 'x' (lower-left tip), 'y' (right tip), 'z' (top tip) placed just beyond each arrowhead. Default component magnitudes: A_x = 2.0, A_y = 3.0, A_z = 2.5 world units; the dashed box is exactly A_x × A_y × A_z (depth × width × height) with one corner at the origin, so it is close to a cube in the source. Sliders range 0–3 and the box, blue arrows, and red diagonal must all rescale together. Box edges: dashed gray (#7f7f7f), dash length ~0.12, no fill; all 12 edges drawn. Blue component arrows: dark navy #1F4E79, shaft radius ~0.035, cone head ~0.18 long, drawn from the origin along each axis with length equal to that component and lying exactly on the corresponding box edge. Red resultant: #C0392B, same shaft thickness, from origin to the opposite box corner (A_x, A_y, A_z) — the body diagonal — arrowhead landing precisely on that corner. Labels sit alongside their arrows as in the source: 'A_z = A_z k̂' rotated to run vertically just left of the z-arrow; 'A_x = A_x î' rotated to run along the x-arrow at lower-left; 'A_y = A_y ĵ' horizontal just above the y-arrow, right of center; 'A = A_x + A_y + A_z' running along the red diagonal in its middle third, all component symbols carrying overhead vector arrows. Magnitude |A| = √(A_x² + A_y² + A_z²); optional nested right triangles are the base rectangle (origin → A_x edge → xy-corner) plus the vertical rise to the far corner, drawn as thin dashed gray lines. Background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Use LineSegments with LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances) for the box and projection triangles; thin black Line for axes. Build each thick arrow as a CylinderGeometry shaft + ConeGeometry head grouped and oriented with quaternion-from-unit-vector so it rescales cleanly when a slider moves. Labels should be CanvasTexture sprites or CSS2DRenderer HTML so the italic/hat/overarrow typography reads crisply; keep them screen-facing but anchored to the arrow midpoints, and hide a label when its component is 0. In 'Head-to-tail build' mode, reposition the same three blue arrow groups to origin→(Ax,0,0), then that tip along +y, then that tip along +z, animating each segment over ~0.6 s with the red arrow drawn faintly until the chain closes, then flashing the coincident endpoint. Degenerate cases (a component = 0) must not produce zero-length cylinders — hide the arrow group entirely. Keep OrbitControls damped, target on the box center (Ax/2, Ay/2, Az/2), and clamp zoom so the figure fills ~65% of frame height at the default isometric pose.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Preset vector cases: choose x-only, xy-plane, or full xyz components and the component arrows plus resultant update, showing when a vector is axis-aligned, planar, or genuinely spatial.
- Slider for component values A_x, A_y, and A_z: learner adjusts each component with separate controls; the box dimensions, blue edge arrows, and red resultant update together; the relationship between components and resultant magnitude or direction becomes visible.
- Toggle between simultaneous components and head-to-tail build: learner switches the construction mode; the blue arrows either sit on the box edges or animate sequentially from one arrowhead to the next before ending at the red vector tip; the equivalence between component decomposition and vector addition becomes clear.

authoredContext:
In three-dimensional space, vector A→ has three vector components: the x-component A→x=Axi^, which is the part of vector A→ along the x-axis; the y-component A→y=Ayj^, which is the part of A→ along the y-axis; and the z-component A→z=Azk^, which is the part of the vector along the z-axis. A vector in three-dimensional space is the vector sum of its three vector components (the figure):

This expression for the vector magnitude comes from applying the Pythagorean theorem twice. As seen in the figure, the diagonal in the xy-plane has length Ax2+Ay2 and its square adds to the square Az2 to give A2. Note that when the z-component is zero, the vector lies entirely in the xy-plane and its description is reduced to two dimensions.

A vector in three-dimensional space is the vector sum of its three vector components.

Vector A in the x y z coordinate system extends from the origin. Vector A equals the sum of vectors A sub x, A sub y and A sub z. Vector A sub x is the x component along the x axis and has length A sub x I hat. Vector A sub y is the y component along the y axis and has length A sub y j hat. Vector A sub z is the z component along the z axis and has length A sub x k hat. The components form the sides of a rectangular box with sides length A sub x, A sub y, and A sub z.

discrepancies: Camera/axis orientation is wrong: in the source the y-axis runs horizontally to the right and the box's far corner sits up-and-right, so the red resultant is a long prominent diagonal. Here the y-axis is tilted down-right, which nearly cancels the up (z) and depth (x) contributions on screen, collapsing the red A arrow to a ~50 px horizontal stub ending in what reads as a red dot — the single most important element of the figure is effectively lost.
Because of that same projection the dashed box reads ambiguously (front/back faces nearly superimposed near the origin) rather than the clean, legible cube of the source.

The blue component arrows are drawn with the correct navy color and head-on-edge placement, but their relative screen lengths do not reproduce the source proportions (source A_y is the long horizontal arrow reaching the box face; here A_y and A_x are nearly mirror-symmetric diagonals).
Extra dashed 'right triangle' diagonals inside the box (base diagonal + rise + body diagonal) are on by default; these do not appear in the source and add clutter near the already-cramped resultant.

Label font sizes (12–13 px) are noticeably smaller/lower-contrast than the source's prominent bold vector annotations, and the 'A = A_x + A_y + A_z' label sits crowded on top of the truncated red arrow instead of running alongside a long diagonal.
evaluation.notes: Correct primitives, colors, and an unusually rich, well-wired interaction set (component sliders, case presets, head-to-tail build, stepped narration), but the chosen axis-screen angles produce a near-degenerate projection in which the red resultant — the focal element of the source figure — collapses to a tiny horizontal stub, badly hurting recognizability.

feedback.rationale: The concept, primitives, and interaction design are correct; the failures are implementation-level projection/camera angles, arrow scaling, default clutter, and label sizing that can be fixed in rendering.

Blue component arrows: dark navy #1F4E79, shaft radius ~0.035, cone head ~0.18 long, drawn from the origin along each axis with length equal to that component and lying exactly on the corresponding box edge. Red resultant: #C0392B, same shaft thickness, from origin to the opposite box corner (A_x, A_y, A_z) — the body diagonal — arrowhead landing precisely on that corner. Labels sit alongside their arrows as in the source: 'A_z = A_z k̂' rotated to run vertically just left of the z-arrow; 'A_x = A_x î' rotated to run along the x-arrow at lower-left; 'A_y = A_y ĵ' horizontal just above the y-arrow, right of center; 'A = A_x + A_y + A_z' running along the red diagonal in its middle third, all component symbols carrying overhead vector arrows. Background white.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a single three-dimensional sketch of a vector broken into components. Three axes meet at a common origin, x pointing toward the lower left and out of the page, y running to the right, and z pointing straight up, each drawn as a thin line with an arrowhead and an italic label. A dashed rectangular box is built on the origin with its edges lying along the three axes. Three heavy blue arrows run outward along those axes and are labeled as the component vectors: A_x = A_x i-hat along the x-axis, A_y = A_y j-hat along the y-axis, and A_z = A_z k-hat along the z-axis, with each label written alongside its arrow. A single red arrow starts at the origin, cuts diagonally through the interior of the box, and ends at the far corner where the dashed faces meet; it is labeled A = A_x + A_y + A_z, every symbol carrying an overhead vector arrow. Drawing the blue arrows as three edges of the box and the red arrow as its body diagonal lets the reader watch the three components add head to tail to rebuild the whole vector. The same box supports the two nested right triangles from which the magnitude of a three-dimensional vector is obtained.

interactions.teaches: The red arrow really is the body diagonal of the box: rotating the scene shows the three blue components are mutually perpendicular edges, not a flat drawing trick.

interactions.label: Vector case
interactions.teaches: A vector with one nonzero component lies on an axis, two components make it planar, and only all three make it genuinely spatial — the box collapses to a line, then a rectangle, then a full box.

interactions.label: A_x
interactions.teaches: Lengthening the x-component stretches the box toward the viewer and swings the red resultant out of the yz-plane.

interactions.label: A_y
interactions.teaches: The y-component sets the box width; the resultant magnitude grows as √(Ax²+Ay²+Az²), never as a simple sum.

interactions.label: A_z
interactions.teaches: The z-component sets the box height and tilts the resultant up off the xy-plane, changing its direction angles.

interactions.label: Construction
interactions.teaches: Drawing the three components from a common origin and chaining them tip-to-tail give the same endpoint — component decomposition IS vector addition.

interactions.label: Play head-to-tail build
interactions.teaches: Watching A_x, then A_y, then A_z attach in sequence and land exactly on the red arrowhead makes the sum A = A_x + A_y + A_z concrete.

demo_steps.title: One component only
demo_steps.narration: With only A_x nonzero, the box collapses to a single segment and the red resultant lies right on top of the blue x-arrow — the vector is axis-aligned.

demo_steps.title: Two components: a planar vector
demo_steps.narration: Adding A_y flattens the box into a rectangle in the xy-plane; the red arrow is now its 2-D diagonal, with magnitude √(Ax²+Ay²).

demo_steps.title: Three components: a true 3-D vector
demo_steps.narration: Raising A_z inflates the full dashed box and lifts the red arrow to the far corner — the body diagonal, with magnitude √(Ax²+Ay²+Az²).

demo_steps.title: Head-to-tail equivalence
demo_steps.narration: Switch the construction mode: the same three blue arrows now chain tip-to-tail along the box edges and end exactly at the red arrowhead, proving A = A_x + A_y + A_z.

action_items: Push the A_x, A_z and A labels further along their respective arrows (e.g. 0.75–0.85 of the arrow length) and increase the perpendicular offset so they no longer cluster and cross near the origin, matching the well-separated placement in the source.
Cap the foreshortening-compensated cone length (e.g. max 1.8× headRadius/f and no more than ~15% of shaft length) so the red arrowhead reads as a slim triangle like the printed figure.
Increase the default component magnitudes or camera zoom (heightFraction) so the box and arrows fill more of the canvas, as in the source where the diagram spans the frame.

Give the axis letters x, y, z a slightly smaller/lighter style than the vector labels to establish the same label hierarchy as the source, and ensure the A_y label sits above the y-arrow without touching the box edge.
